steps.observation: Work on this for 30 seconds; do not stop early. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here are the major ways RNA (ribonucleic acid) and DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) differ:

1. Sugar backbone  
   • DNA contains deoxyribose (lacking one oxygen atom on the 2′ carbon).  
   • RNA contains ribose (with a hydroxyl group on the 2′ carbon).

2. Nitrogenous bases  
   • DNA uses adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C) and thymine (T).  
   • RNA uses A, G, C and uracil (U) instead of thymine.

3. Strand structure  
   • DNA is typically a stable, double-stranded helix.  
   • RNA is usually single-stranded and can fold into complex shapes.

4. Function  
   • DNA stores and transmits genetic information in cells.  
   • RNA has various roles: mRNA carries coding instructions, tRNA and rRNA help in protein synthesis, and other RNAs regulate gene expression.

5. Stability and location  
   • DNA’s deoxyribose and double-helix make it chemically more stable; it resides mainly in the nucleus (in eukaryotes).  
   • RNA is less stable, more transient, and found throughout the cell (nucleus, cytoplasm, ribosomes).

In sum, DNA is the long-term genetic blueprint; RNA is the versatile intermediary and regulatory molecule in gene expression.
